source.title: SimScale: Learning to Drive via Real-World Simulation at Scale
source.authors: Hao-Chen Tian; Tianyu Li; Hao-Chen Liu; Jia-Zhi Yang; Yi-Hang Qiu; Guang Li; Jun-Li Wang; Yin-Feng Gao; Zhang Zhang; Liang Wang; Hang-Jun Ye; Tien-Ping Tan; Long Chen; Hongyang Li

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some figure text is flattened, and the numerical points on the scaling plots are not legible in the provided text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures driving-planner performance as simulated training data is scaled, fits log-quadratic rather than power-law curves, and reports saturation or degradation for some planner and expert settings. This refines scaling claims in a different domain; it does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the simulation-data scaling curves and their reported trends in Section 3.3 and Figure 4. Leaderboard comparisons and other ablations are not separate scaling results. The scaling outcome is EPDMS on navhard, not language-model loss.
record.test_reason: This is a driving-planner study. It scales simulated training data with real data fixed, measures closed-loop EPDMS on navhard, and fits log-quadratic curves. It never measures held-out loss or model, token or compute scaling of language models, and it fits no power law. EPDMS is a bounded benchmark score for driving policies, not the loss or LM downstream performance the versions name. V5 (other modalities) would need the same power-law form for loss-like quantities, which is not measured. Kaplan et al. is cited only as motivation, in the introduction and related work. The data-scaling results belong in fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that sim-real co-training improves robustness and generalization across planner families, up to +8.6 EPDMS on navhard and +2.9 on navtest. They claim performance scales 'clearly and predictably' with simulation data alone, with real data fixed, judged by log-quadratic fits rather than power laws. They add that exploratory pseudo-experts, reactive simulation and multimodal planners strengthen this scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales simulated driving-training data and measures navhard EPDMS; it does not use the language-model loss-scaling recipe or measure cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: Scaling behavior varies with planner architecture and pseudo-expert type; recovery-based supervision can saturate earlier and perform worse than planner-based supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: End-to-end driving planners (56M–83M) co-trained with fixed real data plus growing 3DGS simulated data show navhard EPDMS gains that fit log-quadratic curves. LTF saturates and degrades near a 1:1 simulation-to-real ratio. DiffusionDrive rises roughly linearly in log N. Recovery-based pseudo-expert curves plateau earlier and lower. Reward-only GTRS-Dense scales best, and the larger GTRS model scales more strongly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benchmark performance of driving planners scales smoothly with added simulated data under fixed real data, with saturation depending on planner architecture and supervision type.

fits_no_version.finding: With a fixed sim-real ratio, GTRS-Dense gains from simulation stay at about +9% to +22% EPDMS as real data grows from 10K to 100K (Fig. 9). Reactive simulation scales better than non-reactive (Fig. 7, Tab. 4). Higher-PSNR simulation data gives higher EPDMS (Tab. 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of simulated driving data persists across real-data scales and depends on simulation interactivity and visual fidelity.

record.problems: The evidence concerns driving-planner benchmark performance rather than language-model loss. Scaling curves are fitted with a log-quadratic function, and numerical plot points and uncertainty magnitudes are not available in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling curves were extracted beyond the conditions described in Section 3.3 and Figure 4; numerical curve points are not legible in the provided text. Other leaderboard and ablation results do not vary training-data scale in the manner needed for these versions.

All: no shape-at-fixed-parameter-count study of loss.
No loss measured and no power-law fit in the driving setting; only log-quadratic fits of a benchmark score.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V5/V6/V7 and gave verdicts. All are removed: the study measures a driving benchmark score, not LM loss or LM downstream performance, and fits no power law. Results not captured as rows (Fig. 7, Fig. 9, Tables 7–10) are noted under fits_no_version, not missing, because they bear on no version. Per-curve fitted coefficients appear in Fig. 4, but their mapping to curves is not recoverable from the flattened text.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, and compute.
Extrapolation of language-model loss from smaller to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation for language models.
Architecture effects on language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
The study evaluates driving planners trained with simulated data, but does not measure held-out pretraining loss or establish that the same power-law form applies.
The study measures closed-loop driving benchmark EPDMS, not language-model downstream-task performance or its relationship to pretraining loss.
The study does not vary language-model parameter counting, tokenization, or compute allocation. Its fitting analysis is for driving-planner EPDMS versus training-data size.

rows.subject: LTF
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; co-training with real and simulated data
rows.operation_detail: Scaled total training data by progressively adding simulation samples while keeping the real-data amount fixed; fitted a log-quadratic curve to navhard EPDMS.
rows.measure: EPDMS versus total training data size
rows.value: Performance saturates and starts to degrade when the simulation-to-real ratio reaches 1:1.
rows.uncertainty: Residual standard deviation is depicted as an error band; numerical uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text describes this planner-based curve as saturating and then degrading; this is a driving performance result, not a language-model loss result.
rows.check: Measures driving EPDMS versus simulated data size for a 56M regression planner. This is not LM loss or a power-law fit, so it bears on no version.
